title: Remove EOL platform: Debian 12 (bookworm)
description:
Remove the Debian 12 (bookworm) images now that the platform is reaching end of life, following the same approach used for the recent focal/R 4.0 removal.

## Changes

- Delete all `bookworm` image directories across R versions (4.2-4.6, devel, next) and `base/bookworm`.
- Remove `bookworm` from `update.sh` (OS identifier map and the debian template case).
- Remove `bookworm` from `VARIANTS` in the `Makefile`.
- Drop the Debian 12 row from the supported distributions table in `README.md`.

Re-ran `./update.sh` to confirm no `bookworm` artifacts are regenerated and no references remain.

title: Initial support for ARM64 images
description:
Resolves https://github.com/rstudio/r-docker/issues/75

Adds initial support for arm64 images as multiarch images with the same tags (`posit/r-base:4.5-noble` for both x86_64 and arm64). I recommend reviewing by commit because there's one commit with a ton of auto-generated file updates.

- Add support for building arm64 images, except CentOS 7, because TinyTeX is not currently supported there.
  - Updates to the R installation, TinyTeX, and Pandoc installation to determine the arch to install
- Update GHA to build and publish arm64 images as multiarch images.
- Rework GHA publishing to keep build times down - instead of double-building images for the rstudio org and posit org, only build images once, then publish to both orgs at the same time. But only do this for the x86 images - arm64 images are not published to `rstudio`
  - Also removed some of the old `post_push` and `docker-compose.test.yml` files that were intended for Docker Hub CI use. The post_push script was still used to re-tag images with their version alias. This wasn't flexible enough to handle the new complicated build matrix with multiarch images, so I replaced these with a simple `version.txt` file, which a new publishing script uses to push the right tags + tag aliases.

I've pushed some test images already to verify that this works: https://hub.docker.com/repository/docker/posit/r-base/tags

---


For future work:
- We should introduce image caching to speed builds up further and make them more reliable. Right now, the images are always built without cache since they've been quick fast, but the arm64 additions have made builds longer and more flaky because TinyTeX has to be built from source currently. And those source builds seem to fail often from random transient errors.
  - To use docker buildx caching, we'll need to merge the base dockerfiles and R dockerfiles together, because buildx doesn't support build images off a local docker image (seems odd that this isn't supported, but :shrug:)

title: Add find command to rockylinux8 base image
description:
`find` is usually installed by default, but not on RHEL/Rocky 8's base image. In this specific case, the s2 package needs it for its config script: https://github.com/r-spatial/s2/blob/1764fe73e54556b98c721df6a8e83d93bf02d83b/configure#L98-L99

find is never specified as a system requirement either, so the best place is probably here in the base image.

Add `R-next` images, similar to how we have `R-devel` images. `R-next` is the next version of R which switches from alpha to beta to RC, added to the R builds a while back: https://github.com/rstudio/r-builds/pull/116

It's useful for testing minor R version releases before the release day, and I've been using these locally for R 4.4.0 testing. So adding these images, but not documenting them or enabling daily builds for them. When needed for testing, they can be rebuilt on demand with the GHA workflow.

    - jammy: 2.9.2
    - centos7: 1.12.3
    - rockylinux8: 2.0.6 (powertools)

title: Migrate to GitHub Actions; work around Dockerfile caching bug
description:
There are two separate but related changes here:

1. Migrate from CircleCI to GitHub Actions. CircleCI has worked really well, but it seems like we're converging on GHA in the org, so less YAML config to learn means easier maintenance. The CircleCI config has also had a lot of copy-paste redundancy that made it a bit harder to maintain, and I even forgot to update it with the new Rocky 9 and SUSE 15.4 builds in https://github.com/rstudio/r-docker/pull/85. With GHA, we can take advantage of a few nice features:
   - The build matrix is now dynamic generated from the Makefile, so no more need to update the config when adding new platforms.
   - The build matrix is still parallelized by platform, but we could easily parallelize by R version as well if the build time gets longer, like in R-builds. Build times aren't an issue yet though.
   - The manual workflow trigger is more powerful in GHA than in CircleCI. The CircleCI console doesn't support parameters (last I checked), but GHA does, so we can now manually run builds with options to limit platforms/versions, disable publishing, and rebuild the full patch version matrix.
   - The CRON jobs to build R-devel daily or patch versions monthly are now configured in separate files (and can be manually triggered individually) for a little better organization. This is using GHA's [reusable workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/reusing-workflows), which just requires an `on.workflow_call` section. Inputs have to be duplicated with `workflow_dispatch`, but you can refer to both inputs using `input.<param>` in the workflow.

2. Work around a Dockerfile caching bug with Docker BuildKit: https://github.com/moby/buildkit/issues/1368. There's a really bad bug where `docker build` can use the wrong Dockerfile for caching, even if the content is different, because the timestamp and file sizes of two Dockerfiles are the same. This caused https://github.com/rstudio/r-docker/issues/86 while I was testing publishing, which I thought would be safe enough.

The issue looks like this - note the incorrectly cached step of downloading R 3.5.3 in the `3.6-focal` build:
https://github.com/rstudio/r-docker/actions/runs/3041017846/jobs/4897712035

And finally, the builds do fail on openSUSE 15.4 right now because there's no R-devel build for SUSE 15.4. Otherwise, we could skip the build or look into a workaround for the R-devel problem.

title: Build and maintain R patch versions
description:
- Adds support for building R patch versions
- Adds a CI job that rebuilds all patch versions once a month, so that they're actively maintained and updated with security patches (e.g., Baron Samedit sudo vulnerability). I think this job can also be manually triggered via the CircleCI console if needed.

Currently supported patch versions are just the tags available on Docker Hub, which are R 3.6.0, 3.6.1, 3.6.2, 3.6.3, 4.0.0, 4.0.1, 4.0.2, 4.0.3, and all the latest patch versions from R 3.5 and below. It's a large matrix and the job currently takes 2+ hours, but at least there are only a few R releases a year, and the job only runs once a month. Here's a one-off build I did on another branch: https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/rstudio/r-docker/355/workflows/761bfc85-5d6f-40e8-9c77-22ef9a90c0c1

To build patch versions manually:
```sh
# Build, test, and push R 3.6.0 xenial
make build-3.6.0-xenial
make test-3.6.0-xenial
make push-3.6.0-xenial

# Build, test, and push all R patch versions
INCLUDE_PATCH_VERSIONS=yes make build-all
INCLUDE_PATCH_VERSIONS=yes make test-all
INCLUDE_PATCH_VERSIONS=yes make push-all

# The "all" targets still build just the minor versions by default
make build-all
```

title: Add CircleCI pipeline for automated builds
description:
Adds a CircleCI pipeline that mimics the auto builds on Docker Hub. Images are built and tested for PR and non-master branches, and additionally published for the master branch. This should work with forked pull requests as well, but the CircleCI repo settings should prevent environment variables (Docker Hub credentials) from being leaked.

Docker Hub's auto builds are still faster and have the nice "auto rebuild when base image changes" feature. So right now, I've set up Docker Hub to build the most important images up to the 25 rule limit, base images + R 3.4 to 3.6. While the CircleCI pipeline is set up to build R 3.1 to 3.3. If we want to keep the CircleCI-built images updated regularly, there's a way to schedule jobs: https://circleci.com/docs/2.0/workflows/#scheduling-a-workflow

The pipeline takes 3 environment variables set from the CircleCI repo settings:
- `VERSIONS` - R versions to build, e.g. `"3.1 3.2 3.3"` (the current setting). If empty, all versions are built. If we want to move everything to CircleCI, we can just unset this variable.
- `DOCKER_USER` - Docker Hub user, only used for master branch
- `DOCKER_PASS` - Docker Hub pass, only used for master branch

Since we only get one concurrent job, I've configured each job to build all `VERSIONS` for a single distro, so we reuse the base image as much as possible.

Examples:
- Workflow for this PR: https://circleci.com/workflow-run/a8974e00-93f1-4c3d-939d-bc25b7558111
- Job that publishes to Docker Hub (modified config for testing): https://circleci.com/gh/rstudio/r-docker/110

**Note:** builds use my personal Docker Hub credentials right now, but we'll switch to a service account if we need this to be permanent. Also after this merges, I'd like to try a forked pull request to confirm that CI works and no environment variables are leaked.

title: Add R 3.6.0
description:
This was pretty straightforward, except for CentOS 6 (!!). Packages with C++11 code couldn't be installed:
```sh
+ R CMD INSTALL /test/testpkg --clean
* installing to library '/opt/R/3.6.0/lib/R/library'
* installing *source* package 'testpkg' ...
** using staged installation
** libs
Error in .shlib_internal(args) :
  C++11 standard requested but CXX11 is not defined
* removing '/opt/R/3.6.0/lib/R/library/testpkg'
Makefile:31: recipe for target 'test-3.6-centos6' failed
make: *** [test-3.6-centos6] Error 1
```

In previous versions of R (3.4, 3.5), this `CXX11` Make variable was set to `CXX11 = g++` in the `$R_HOME/etc/Makeconf` file. Since R 3.6.0, I think this is no longer set if the C++ compiler used to compile R doesn't support C++11.

> The options selected for the C++ compiler default to the C++11 standard if supported, otherwise to the C++98 standard.
https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-devel/NEWS.html

> For the use of C++11 and later in R packages see the ‘Writing R Extensions’ manual. Currently the default C++ standard is that of the compiler used: from R 3.6.0 it will be C++11 if supported by the compiler.
https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-admin.html#C_002b_002b-Support

---

We could compile R on CentOS 6 with the newer C++ compiler instead, but I think it'd be better to just add the proper configuration variables here. I've added a CentOS 6 specific Dockerfile template that sets these in the system-wide `$R_HOME/etc/Makevars.site`. The values were copied from the defaults on CentOS 7, and similar to what others have recommended. The tests pass now, but I think we should try building CRAN on 3.6-centos6 to truly test it later.

```sh
# CXX11 Make variables

# 3.6-centos6
$ docker run --rm rstudio/r-base:3.6-centos6 cat $(R RHOME)/etc/Makeconf | grep CXX11
CXX11 = 
CXX11FLAGS =  $(LTO)
CXX11PICFLAGS = 
CXX11STD = 
SHLIB_CXX11LD = $(CXX11) $(CXX11STD)
SHLIB_CXX11LDFLAGS = -shared

# 3.6-centos7
$ docker run --rm rstudio/r-base:3.6-centos7 cat $(R RHOME)/etc/Makeconf | grep CXX11
CXX11 = g++
CXX11FLAGS = -g -O2 $(LTO)
CXX11PICFLAGS = -fpic
CXX11STD = -std=gnu++11
SHLIB_CXX11LD = $(CXX11) $(CXX11STD)
SHLIB_CXX11LDFLAGS = -shared
```

#### References
- Similar issue on MRO 3.4 with the same solution: https://github.com/Microsoft/microsoft-r-open/issues/26#issuecomment-311682482
- Docs for each Make variable: https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/R-3-6-branch/config.site#L255
- C++ support in R: https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-admin.html#C_002b_002b-Support

title: Set default UTF-8 locale
description:
The Ubuntu images currently set a default UTF-8 locale (`LANG=C.UTF-8`), but the CentOS and openSUSE images don't (defaults to `LANG=C`). This sets a default UTF-8 locale in each base image and adds an R test to confirm that. 

Note that the default locales that come with Ubuntu, openSUSE, and CentOS images are all different. Ubuntu and openSUSE come with `C.UTF-8`, while CentOS only has `en_US.UTF-8` as the closest thing. 

I also slightly changed how the locale was being set on Ubuntu. It was being set through the `Renviron.site` file before, which makes it hard to override. For example, if you wanted to change the locale in a Docker image:
```dockerfile
FROM rstudio/r-base:3.5-xenial

ENV LANG pt_BR.UTF-8
```
The locale wouldn't change in R since the `Renviron.site` file takes precedence. I've set it through an environment variable in the base image instead, which is consistent with what other Docker images do.

#### References
- Locale discussion in the rocker images: https://github.com/rocker-org/rocker/issues/19
- How locales are set in some of the official Docker images:
  - https://github.com/docker-library/python/blob/4e284ff8ad5458518743188afa3e64d83ea9986c/3.8-rc/stretch/Dockerfile#L14
  - https://github.com/docker-library/docs/blob/3e578ee6c54631939dd66570c1415ff0e26dc1a0/ubuntu/content.md#locales
- `C.UTF-8` vs `en_US.UTF-8`: https://community.hpe.com/t5/General/Difference-between-C-utf8-and-en-us-utf8-points/td-p/4418194
- CentOS doesn't have a `C.UTF-8` locale by default: https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=902094

title: Fix text rendering on CentOS 6
description:
Text rendering is currently broken on CentOS 6 because there aren't any system fonts installed. For example, you just get boxes and this Pango warning when generating a plot:
```sh

(process:23): Pango-WARNING **: failed to choose a font, expect ugly output. engine-type='PangoRenderFc', script='latin'

(process:23): Pango-WARNING **: failed to choose a font, expect ugly output. engine-type='PangoRenderFc', script='common'
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20401866/56675940-deb9a200-6682-11e9-9a12-47e135c6fa93.png)

Listing installed fonts on CentOS 6/7 shows that CentOS 6 has no fonts, while CentOS 7 has DejaVu Sans installed by default. 

title: Add missing time zone database on xenial/bionic
description:
Time zone conversions weren't working since the Ubuntu xenial/bionic images don't come with time zone data, which R looks for at `/usr/share/zoneinfo`.
```r
> format(Sys.time(), usetz = TRUE)
[1] "2019-03-18 15:44:06 UTC"

> format(Sys.time(), usetz = TRUE, tz = "America/Chicago")
[1] "2019-03-18 15:44:13 America"

> OlsonNames()  # time zone names
character(0)
Warning message:
In OlsonNames() : no Olson database found
```

The Ubuntu images used to include the `tzdata` package but not anymore (https://github.com/docker-library/official-images/issues/2863), so adding it here. Time zone conversions should work now:
```r
> format(Sys.time(), usetz = TRUE)
[1] "2019-03-18 15:46:31 UTC"

> format(Sys.time(), usetz = TRUE, tz = "America/Chicago")
[1] "2019-03-18 10:46:37 CDT"

> head(OlsonNames())
[1] "Africa/Abidjan"     "Africa/Accra"       "Africa/Addis_Ababa"
[4] "Africa/Algiers"     "Africa/Asmara"      "Africa/Asmera"
```
